title: Argument
body:
An **argument** is a set of statements where some, the premises, are offered as support for one
further statement, the conclusion. Logic evaluates the connection between them and takes no
position on whether the premises are true.

```
Premise:     Every course with a lab meets twice a week.
Premise:     PHYS 1201 has a lab.
Conclusion:  PHYS 1201 meets twice a week.
```

Words such as therefore, so, thus and hence mark the conclusion, and since, because and given
that mark a premise. Neither marker is required, so identifying which statement is being argued
for is the first step and is done by asking what the passage is trying to convince you of.

Not every group of statements is an argument. An explanation says why something already
accepted is the case, and a description asserts several things without offering any as support
for another. See [[Logical Validity]] for what makes an argument work and [[Soundness]]
for what makes it worth accepting.
